text: Boolean algebra says A && B equals B && A. How can Java violate that?
choices: Evaluation can stop partway, so one order may crash before producing a value
&& is not really a boolean operator in Java
Java evaluates operands in an unspecified order
It does not; the two are always interchangeable
explanation: The law holds for expressions that terminate normally. s != null && s.length() > 0 is safe and the reverse throws. A useful way to hold it: && and || are control flow closer to if than to AND, which happen to produce a boolean.
